high.title: Peso Tumbles to Over Three-Week Low
high.summary: The Philippine Peso depreciated sharply by 26.1 centavos, closing at P61.621 against the USD — its weakest level in over three weeks, last seen on June 8 when it settled at P61.69. The selloff was driven by two key catalysts: renewed hawkish expectations surrounding the US Federal Reserve and persistent geopolitical risk premiums stemming from ongoing Middle East conflict, both of which fueled broad USD demand. For FX traders, this move signals that the PHP remains vulnerable to external headwinds, particularly any upside surprises in US economic data or Fed communication that reinforces a higher-for-longer rate narrative. The breach of the P61.50 level is technically significant and warrants close monitoring — a sustained move toward P61.69 and beyond could open the door to further depreciation. Bond investors should watch for any pass-through effects on inflation expectations, which could complicate the BSP's easing calculus. The BSP's intervention posture and its TDF operations (see below) will be critical near-term signals to watch.

high.title: TDF Yield Climbs on Hawkish BSP, Fed
high.summary: The BSP's seven-day Term Deposit Facility (TDF) auction saw yields rise amid hawkish monetary policy expectations from both the BSP and the US Federal Reserve, reinforcing a tightening bias in short-end Philippine rates. Total bids reached P146.927 billion against a P110 billion offer, keeping the facility heavily oversubscribed — a signal of ample system liquidity but also strong market appetite for BSP instruments at higher yields. The oversubscription (at 1.34x cover) reflects banks parking excess liquidity defensively in the face of FX and rate uncertainty. For bond investors, the upward drift in TDF yields is a key leading indicator for the broader government securities curve — rising TDF rates typically exert upward pressure on short-to-medium tenor GS yields. Combined with the Peso's weakness, this TDF print reinforces a hawkish near-term rates environment and reduces the probability of a near-term BSP rate cut. Traders should recalibrate duration exposure accordingly and monitor the next Monetary Board meeting for any shift in forward guidance.

high.title: Bond Yields Go Down as Oil's Drop Eases Inflation Worries
high.summary:
The Bureau of the Treasury (BTr) conducted a fully awarded auction of reissued 7-year Treasury bonds, raising P30 billion as planned at a **lower average yield**, with total bids reaching P65.135 billion — more than **2x oversubscribed**. The rally in bonds was driven by easing inflation expectations following a decline in global oil prices, itself catalyzed by progress toward a Middle East peace deal. The strong bid-to-cover ratio signals robust domestic demand for government paper, suggesting that investors are positioning for a continued disinflationary environment and potential BSP easing ahead. For bond investors, the lower clearing yield and oversubscription are bullish signals — duration positioning in the belly of the curve (7-year tenor) appears well-supported. For FX traders, lower inflation expectations reduce pressure on the BSP to maintain restrictive policy, which could weigh modestly on PHP carry appeal over the medium term. **Key watch:** Upcoming June CPI print and BSP's next rate decision, which will determine whether this yield compression has further room to run.

---

medium.title: BSP Says Wholesale CBDCs Can Reduce Transaction Costs, Lags
medium.summary:
The BSP's Project Agila pilot report highlights wholesale CBDC (wCBDC) potential for cross-border payments, remittances, institutional transfers, and financial securities settlement — all areas with direct macro-financial relevance for the Philippines. For FX and remittance flows, a more efficient wCBDC infrastructure could over time reduce friction costs in OFW remittance channels, potentially improving the predictability and volume of FX inflows that traditionally support the Peso. From a capital markets perspective, improved securities settlement efficiency could enhance foreign investor participation in Philippine GS markets. While this remains a medium-to-long-term structural story rather than an immediate market mover, fund managers with a longer horizon should track Project Agila's progress as it could meaningfully impact PHP liquidity dynamics and bond market accessibility.

medium.title: PHL Posts Net Hot Money Inflow in May
medium.summary: Foreign portfolio investments (FPI) registered with the BSP posted a **net inflow of $232.46 million in May**, reversing two consecutive months of net outflows and signaling a recovery in risk appetite toward Philippine assets. However, the figure remains significantly below the $600.77 million net inflow recorded in the same month a year prior, indicating that while sentiment has stabilized, foreign investor conviction is not yet fully restored. The swing from a **$1.601 billion net outflow** in the prior month to positive territory is a meaningful directional shift and provides near-term support for the PHP. For FX traders, sustained FPI inflows act as a natural demand driver for the peso, though the year-on-year decline highlights structural headwinds. **Key watch:** Whether inflows accelerate in June/July as global risk sentiment evolves, and any BSP commentary on capital flow trends.

medium.title: Philippine GDP Likely Grew 2.6% in Q2, Says UA&P
medium.summary: The University of Asia and the Pacific (UA&P) estimates Philippine Q2 2026 GDP growth decelerated sharply to **2.6%**, weighed down by elevated inflation and weakening domestic demand. The report acknowledges early signs of recovery momentum but flags a constrained outlook. A GDP print at this level would represent a significant slowdown and could strengthen the case for BSP rate cuts to support growth, which would be **bearish for PHP** but **bullish for Philippine government bonds**. For PSEi investors, sluggish growth raises concerns about corporate earnings momentum. **Key watch:** The official Q2 GDP release and the BSP's policy response, particularly any forward guidance on the rate path.

medium.title: NCR Retail Price Growth Slows to 2-Month Low in May
medium.summary: Metro Manila's General Retail Price Index (GRPI) rose 4.0% year-on-year in May, decelerating from 4.5% month-on-month in April and marking the slowest pace in two months. The easing was primarily driven by softening prices of mineral fuels and lubricants. While this is a sub-national and retail-level metric rather than the headline CPI, it signals a tentative moderation in consumer price pressures in the country's key economic hub. For PHP and rates traders, this reading is a secondary data point worth monitoring: a sustained deceleration in retail inflation could reinforce the BSP's easing bias and provide cover for further policy rate cuts, which would be modestly peso-negative at the margin. Watch for the national May CPI print and any BSP commentary on the inflation trajectory before drawing firm conclusions.

medium.title: Philippine Shares Rebound as Investors Pick Up Bargains
medium.summary: The PSEi recovered on Wednesday, gaining 0.53% (+32.09 points) to close at 6,069.26, following the prior session's sharp 1.56% sell-off. Sentiment was supported by bargain hunting and optimism surrounding US-Iran diplomatic negotiations, which eased geopolitical risk appetite. The rebound was technically driven rather than fundamental, suggesting fragile sentiment. Foreign participation data and net buying/selling flows should be monitored to assess whether this represents genuine risk-on re-entry or merely a technical correction within a broader downtrend.

medium.title: Philippine Stocks Drop on Uncertainty Over US-Iran Talks
medium.summary: The PSEi fell 1.56% (-96.24 points) to 6,037.17 on Tuesday, with the broader All Shares index also declining 1.0% to 3,319.29. The sell-off was attributed to geopolitical uncertainty around US-Iran negotiations and a weakening local economic outlook, which dampened investor confidence and triggered profit-taking. The move highlights the PSEi's vulnerability to external risk factors, particularly global oil price dynamics that can simultaneously pressure the PHP via import costs and widen the current account deficit. A sustained geopolitical risk premium in oil markets warrants close attention for its knock-on FX and inflationary implications.
